is msg actually bad for you

MSG is monosodium glutamate, and glutamate turns up naturally in tomatoes, cheese, mushrooms and seaweed — it is basically what savoury tastes like. Some people report mild, short-lived symptoms from very large doses. why is pluto not a planet anymore

Pluto didn't change — the rulebook did. ❄️ In 2006 astronomers agreed that a planet must circle the Sun, be round, and sweep its own orbital lane clear of other stuff. Pluto shares its lane with many icy rocks, so it got a new name: dwarf planet. Still out there, still interesting. 🪐 [CHIPS]What's a dwarf planet|More about Pluto|Other dwarf planets[/CHIPS]
why do some sunglasses cut the glare off the road and others just go dark

Light bouncing off a flat road or a water surface comes away mostly wobbling one way, side to side. That is the glare. Ordinary dark lenses dim everything equally, glare included. Polarised lenses work like a letterbox slot, passing the up-and-down wobble and stopping the side-to-side one, so the shine drops away while the rest of the view stays bright. 😎[QUIZ]Which surface throws the worst glare?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]A brick wall|Wet road at noon|A dark curtain[/CHIPS]

explain the monty hall problem to me

Three doors, a prize behind one. You pick a door, then the host — who knows where the prize is — opens a losing door and offers you a swap. Switch, and you win two times out of three. Your first pick was right only a third of the time, and the host's knowledge shoves the rest of the odds onto the one door left. 🚪

[CHIPS]Why not fifty fifty|Test it with cards|What if host guesses[/CHIPS]

is there a name for those flat sheet clouds covering the whole sky

White glue is a crowd of tiny plastic-like particles floating in water 🧪. why does cardboard go weak the moment it gets wet
